title: Navajo Nation Judicial Branch — Treaty of 1 June 1868, Article II
license: Underlying United States treaty text is public domain. Geometry is an original generalized reconstruction of factual geographic terms, not copied from a tribal GIS or map.
note: Treaty signed 1 June, ratification advised 25 July, proclaimed 12 August 1868. Article II specifies 37°N, the latitude of old Fort Defiance, the meridian of Fort Lyon/Bear Spring and an approximate 109°30′W western limit subject to inclusion of the whole Canyon de Chelly and its outlet. The rendered version starts at proclamation; signature and return are separate events. Article XI addresses return, not a precise boundary change date. Checked 15 November 2026.

title: Rutherford B. Hayes — Executive Order—Defining Boundaries for Navajo Indians, 29 October 1878
license: Underlying federal executive order and Kappler's 1904 government publication are public domain. No website design or proprietary geometry is reproduced.
note: American Presidency Project transcription citing Kappler I, pp. 875–876. Adds the tract from the original northwest corner west to 110°W, south to 36°N and east to the old boundary. Used to reconstruct the union with the earlier reserved footprint. Checked 15 November 2026.

title: Rutherford B. Hayes — Executive Order: Navajo Reserve, 6 January 1880
license: Underlying federal executive order is public domain. This project draws its own generalized interpretation of the geographic facts.
note: Oklahoma State University primary-document transcription. Adds land along the San Juan River to a line 15 miles east of the old eastern boundary and south to a line 6 miles beyond the old southern boundary, extending west to 110°W. A straight river chord is explicitly a display generalization, not recovered 1880 channel geometry. Checked 15 November 2026.

title: Chester A. Arthur — Executive Order—Added Navajo Lands, 17 May 1884 (exclusion amendment)
license: Underlying federal executive order is public domain; chronology only, no external geometry copied.
note: Despite the archive page title, this particular order excludes portions of T29N R14–16W south of the San Juan River from the 1880 addition. Other orders of that date enlarged the reservation elsewhere. It establishes that the 1880 outline must not be extended unchanged through 1934. The later parcel geometry is not included. Checked 15 November 2026.

title: National Park Service — Canyon de Chelly National Monument, National Register documentation
license: Underlying federal National Park Service documentation is public domain. Modern geographic references are used only to locate the treaty's named canyon, not to copy a modern reservation boundary.
note: The location documentation places the western canyon area west of 109°30′W. This corroborates the need to respect Article II's outlet proviso; the nominal meridian alone is insufficient. The 109.55°W display line is a disclosed coarse interpretation, not the claimed result of an 1868 cadastral survey. Checked 15 November 2026.

title: Chester A. Arthur — Executive Order—Establishment of Moqui (Hopi) Reserve, 16 December 1882
license: Underlying federal executive order and Kappler's 1904 government publication are public domain. The rectangle is an original rendering of the order's coordinate facts.
note: Kappler I, p. 805. The western meridian is 111°W, not 111°30′W; north and south are 36°30′N and 35°30′N. The order also provides for other Indians whom the Secretary might settle there. It does not support an exclusive Hopi occupancy claim or a retroactive later partition. Checked 15 November 2026.

title: United States — Act of 14 June 1934, 48 Stat. 960–962
license: United States statute, public domain. Used for the historical status statement, not for copied third-party geometry.
note: The statute defining Navajo exterior boundaries in Arizona expressly states on p. 961 that the existing status of the Moqui (Hopi) reservation created in 1882 is unaffected. Supports retaining that 1882 footprint to the atlas's 1934 cutoff. Does not support extending the earlier 1880 Navajo outline unchanged. Checked 15 November 2026.
